explanation: Convert the input BSTs in place to circular sorted doubly linked lists, break their circular endpoints, merge their forward chains, and construct a new midpoint BST from the merged list cursor.
timeComplexity: O(m+n): each conversion, merge and reconstruction visits nodes linearly.
spaceComplexity: O(m+n) including newly allocated output nodes; recursive conversion additionally needs up to O(hA+hB) stack, and balanced rebuilding O(log(m+n+1)).

correctness: Recursive list conversion preserves inorder; merging preserves every occurrence in sorted order. Building a left half, reading the next value for a fresh root, and building the remaining half produces exactly the specified midpoint structure. Conversion mutates original nodes, but reconstruction allocates new result nodes.
walkthrough: Trees [4,1,7] and [6,2,9] become sorted chains, merged as [1,2,4,6,7,9]. Three values build the left subtree; the next value 6 creates the new root; the last two values build its right subtree. The new tree serializes as [6,2,9,1,4,7].
edgeCases: Either input tree may be empty.
Duplicate values from either input are retained.
The midpoint convention matters because this corpus compares structure.
Input tree child links are repurposed as list links during merging; callers must not expect the original trees to remain intact.
